items.title: Lights-out Luka and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?
items.summary: Luka Dončić has the Lakers at the top of the Western Conference.Photograph: Gina Ferazzi/Los Angeles Times/Getty ImagesOne of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished.Related:…

items.title: Canada Qualifies For 2027 FIBA World Cup
items.summary: The Canadian men’s national team lost its first qualifying game for the 2027 FIBA World Cup on Thursday, falling to Uruguay, 84-78, per Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca (Twitter links). Veteran big man Kelly Olynyk, who has been playing in Italy this season after 13 years in the NBA, had 21 points (on 7-of-11 shooting), six rebounds, three blocks, two steals and two assists in defeat. However, Canada still qualified for next summer’s tournament later in the evening when the Bahamas was blown out by Argentina, Murphy adds. Canada, which is now 8-1 in Group F, is the first country from the Americas to qualify for the 2027 World Cup. Canada is currently ranked fifth in FIBA’s World Rankings after finishing fifth at the 2024 Olympics in Paris and defeating the United States in the third/fourth place game at the 2023 World Cup, resulting in the country’s first bronze medal at the event. items.title: Jeff Weltman Discusses Why Magic Signed Kevin Porter Jr.
items.summary: The Magic signed free agent guard Kevin Porter Jr. on Wednesday amid a 7-10 start to the season. President of basketball operations Jeff Weltman discussed the thinking behind the move later that day in a phone interview with Jason Beede of The Orlando Sentinel. “We’re trying to get better. We’re looking at our team and seeing where we need help,” Weltman said. “You’re never going to find the perfect player to address every need, especially when you’re looking to acquire a player who (was) presently unsigned. It is unique to find a player with Kevin’s level of talent and competitiveness and be able to add him to a roster. “So, for us, it was more, can he help? Does he address needs? items.summary: While LeBron James has posted solid numbers for the Sixers this fall, he has been content to play a secondary role, having entered Wednesday’s game vs. Miami as the team’s fourth-leading scorer. However, he showed last night that he’s still capable of submitting a vintage LeBron performance, as he accumulated 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double as a 76er. items.title: Northwest Notes: Morant, Holiday, Filipowski, Mitchell
items.summary: After playing in the Trail Blazers’ first four games of the season, point guard Ja Morant has been on the shelf since October 29 due to a left hamstring strain. But Morant, who was ruled out for at least four weeks, may not be sidelined for much longer, writes Joe Freeman of The Oregonian (subscription required). As Freeman details, head coach Micah Nori said on Wednesday that Morant has resumed five-on-five work and has a decent chance to return within the next week or so. “I’ll go out on limb and say we’ll see him on this home stand,” Nori said. “He is getting close.” After beating San Antonio on Wednesday in the first game of a five-game home stand, the Blazers will host the Warriors on Friday, the Pelicans on Sunday, the Timberwolves on Tuesday, and the Jazz next Thursday. items.summary: The NBA appears to be further along on a Las Vegas expansion team than it is on a new Seattle franchise, but the general consensus among current club owners is that they’d like to see two new teams enter the league in the same season, rather than doing so one at a time, ESPN’s Brian Windhorst and Ramona Shelburne said on the Hoop Collective podcast (YouTube link; hat tip to RealGM). items.summary: Given that Jaden McDaniels still had three guaranteed years remaining on his current contract entering this season, it came as a bit of a surprise when word broke just ahead of opening night that the Timberwolves had agreed to tack another year onto his deal, signing the forward to a one-year, $40MM extension that will cover the 2029/30 season.
